sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Speed Dipping Production of Powder-Free Synthetic Nitrile Gloves

stage_1.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (Republic of South Africa) — national registration via the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC)
stage_1.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Roman-Dutch Civil Law, English Common Law, African Customary Law, Constitutional Supremacy — Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006)
SACU–US AGOA trade preference (duty-free access; subject to periodic US eligibility determinations)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act, 2008 (Act No. 71 of 2008), ss. 12–19, 66–78; Companies Regulations, 2011 (GN R351), regs. 18–20; read with the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 for SARS registrations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), a juristic entity under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A or 15.1B) filed electronically through CIPC e-Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital applies to a private company; the Act does not prescribe any authorised or paid-up share capital floor or escrow account. The subscriber may capitalise the company with a nominal R1 initial allotment or leave shares unpaid until issued and the consideration is receivable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: CAPE TOWN — FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF GLOVE MANUFACTURING (Pty) LTD: RESOLVED that, as recorded in the minutes of the first meeting of the first and sole director, the company shall: (1) issue and allot 1,000 ordinary shares of R0.01 each to the incorporator in consideration for the subscription amount, subscribing as a private company; (2) adopt as the company’s registered office the premises situated at [physical address], with the postal address shown in the incorporation application; (3) appoint [name] to the office of whole-time director and [name/entity] as company secretary and financial officer; (4) ratify the opening of corporate bank accounts and the execution of contracts, leases and licence forms; and (5) cause CIPC, SARS, UIF and municipal filings to be made without delay, all in accordance with the Companies Act 71 of 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Company Name Reservation Portal (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, the dtic)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the CIPC e-Services portal, select 'New Company Registration' and then 'Company Name Reservation'. Perform an availability search and submit the proposed name 'ZA_PTY_LTD', together with up to three alternative names. The name must not be the same as, or confusingly similar to, an existing trademark or reserved name. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee via the CIPC payment gateway. Retain the reservation reference number for use in the subsequent incorporation application.
required_dossiers: ID or passport of the incorporator
Proof of residential address of the incorporator
List of proposed names (primary and alternatives)
If filing through an agent: signed power of attorney or letter of authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected on grounds of confusion or restriction, file a corrective name reservation with new alternatives, or make representations to CIPC within 20 business days; failure to cure within the query window results in abandonment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the name reservation reference, complete and file the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and the Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A/15.1B) through CIPC e-Services. The MOI must set out authorised share capital, special director appointment rules, share transfer restrictions typical for a (Pty) Ltd, and any subsisting shareholders' agreements. Pay the incorporation fee; CIPC will vet the application and issue a registration certificate with a company number upon approval. Once issued, appoint a resident director or alternate and confirm a registered office within the Republic.
required_dossiers: Copy of ID or passport and address proof of each director and incorporator
Proof of jurisdiction or physical address for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a query, amend the affected fields and resubmit within the CIPC-prescribed period, generally 10 business days. CIPC may refuse registration if document omissions remain; request written reasons and appeal if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Income Tax, VAT and PAYE Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access SARS eFiling and register the newly incorporated company for income tax as a company taxpayer. Monitor the annual turnover threshold before registering for VAT; if taxable turnover exceeds R1 million, or such turnover is anticipated, submit a VAT registration application. If hiring staff, register as an employer for PAYE using the SARS employer registration forms. Obtain a Tax Compliance Status document after registration. Submit provisional tax returns from the relevant financial year.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is returned or queried, correct the underlying data and resubmit within 30 days. Apply for relief from penalties where late registration was caused by SARS delays.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration: UIF and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL), Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Compensation Fund (COIDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as an employer with the UIF using the Department of Employment and Labour's registration portal or Labour Centre. Obtain a UIF employer number and pay monthly UIF contributions, currently 2% of capped remuneration, split equally between employer and employee. Separately, register with the Compensation Fund for COIDA coverage for occupational injuries and diseases, submitting the annual assessment declaration and paying provisional assessments. Maintain an up-to-date employee record.
required_dossiers: SARS employer registration or PAYE number
Identity documents and remuneration details of first employees, or nil return if no employees yet hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, file a late registration request with reasons; penalties may be added if no reasonable explanation is provided. The employer must supply the registered address and an authorised director's signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning and Manufacturing Premises Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The relevant Local Municipality or Metropolitan Municipality – Planning, Building Control and Business Licensing Departments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for municipal zoning approval for the industrial facility, submission of building plans and an occupancy certificate, and a business licence where required under the Business Act 71 of 1991 and local by-laws. Confirm the site is zoned for manufacturing or industrial use. Arrange a structural engineer's certificate and fire clearance prior to occupation. The licence must be obtained before any manufacturing activity begins.
required_dossiers: Title deed or lease agreement for the premises
Architectural or building plans and professional engineer's structural report
Fire safety certificate from the local fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the zoning or licence is refused, request a written decision and appeal to the Municipal Planning Tribunal within 90 days; correct any non-compliances and resubmit if a resubmission option is available.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) – Directorate of Medical Devices; in coordination with the National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS) and the local Municipality for land-use and building approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Licence (MDML) issued by SAHPRA under the Medicines and Related Substances Act, 1965 (Act 101 of 1965), as amended, and SAHPRA's Medical Device Regulatory Framework.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) – Environmental Impact Assessment and Authorisation Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (Scoping and EIA Report) where the glove dipping and curing facility triggers listed activity thresholds under Listing Notices 1 and 2 of the EIA Regulations, 2014 (GN R982 as amended); smaller plants may qualify for Basic Assessment; environmental authorisation is mandatory before construction starts.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance must be achieved with: (a) the National Water Act 36 of 1998 and municipal sewer by-laws for effluent pH 6.0–11.0, COD ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 250 mg/L, ammonia ≤ 10 mg/L and nitrate ≤ 20 mg/L; (b) the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004's atmospheric emission licence (AEL) for VOCs, PM, NOx and specific nitrosamines, with all discharges vented through certified scrubbers; and (c) the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 requiring disposal of spent chemical bath waste at a licensed hazardous waste facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and evacuation certification from the local fire service; municipal building occupancy certificate confirming compliance with the National Building Regulations and Building Standards Act 103 of 1977; structural integrity clearance by an ECSA-registered professional engineer; occupational health and safety compliance certificate under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including an operative PPE programme and chemical exposure monitoring for latex and nitrile dipping lines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal: https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; corporate registration via CIPC data sharing automatically issues income tax reference number
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation with CIPC, SARS automatically issues a company income tax reference number for resident companies. The foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd must complete SARS eFiling registration to confirm particulars, then apply via the 'Register for VAT' channel (VAT 101 form) once turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed the R1 million compulsory threshold (or voluntary from R50,000). Separate registrations are required for PAYE, UIF, SDL (EMP 101) and Customs (SAD500 exporter code via SARS Customs Modernisation). A non-resident sole shareholder is permissible; the company is a tax resident if incorporated in South Africa, and must appoint a SARS-appointed public officer within one month of commencement of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident company (incorporated in ZA) taxed on worldwide income under s9 of Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; no pass-through; branch of non-resident subject to s9D CFC attribution if POEM outside ZA
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election. Available elections: VAT group registration election under s50(1) of VAT Act 89 of 1991; Small Business Corporation (SBC) turnover election under s12E (R20 million turnover cap) for a 27% reduced corporate rate; s11D R&D tax incentive election (150% deduction); s12B(5) election to accelerate write-off of manufacturing plant and machinery; depreciation and capital allowance elections; Transfer Pricing six-month adjustment election; hybrid mismatch automatic adjustment (no election, mandatory); Turnover-based VAT accounting election (s15(2A)) if annual revenue below R50 million.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under VAT Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 compulsory annual taxable turnover threshold (any rolling 12-month period); voluntary registration at R50,000; branch/external company register if making taxable supplies in ZA and turnover exceeds threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance/stamping mandate currently in force. Tax invoices must comply with s20 VAT Act prescribed particulars (vendor name, VAT number, invoice number, date, description, quantity, consideration). SARS accepts e-invoices and EDI submissions; VAT returns filed electronically via eFiling or e@syFile Vendor. Customs export declarations (SAD500) and export clearance must be lodged electronically through the SARS Customs Modernisation platform (EDI or eFiling), with automatic risk-based selectivity but no continuous transactional digital stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under s11(1)(a) VAT Act for movable goods supplied to a non-resident (who is not a vendor, or is a vendor acquiring for enterprise purposes) if goods are exported from the Republic within 90 days of the time of supply and the supplier retains the prescribed documentary proof. Sterile examination nitrile gloves qualify as movable goods; medical/PPE classification does not alter zero-rating. Services connected to movable goods exported (s11(2)(d)) and services to non-residents (s11(2)(l)) are also zero-rated. All zero-rated supplies must be supported by export documentation; failure to export within 90 days triggers 15% VAT charge.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARs Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 bill of entry) with customs clearance stamping
Bill of Lading or airway waybill evidencing physical departure from a South African port/airport, endorsed to foreign consignee
Commercial invoice issued by the (Pty) Ltd supplier showing VAT number and zero-rating reason
Inward remittance certificate / proof of foreign currency payment received from the non-resident purchaser
Packing list and certificate of origin (SADC/EUR.1 where applicable)
Any contract, insurance, or transport documentation proving export within 90 days (required under Interpretation Note 30)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, with domestic banking supervision conducted by the SARB Prudential Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is a managed-float currency with operationally convertible current account transactions routed through SARB Authorised Dealers; capital account transactions remain administratively controlled. A South African (Pty) Ltd owned wholly or partly by non-residents may receive equity capital without minimum statutory capital, but the inward subscription must be reported by the receiving Authorised Dealer under the inward investment reporting framework and must satisfy FICA beneficial ownership verification. Dividend and profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permissible once the dividend is declared in accordance with the Companies Act solvency and liquidity test, South African dividend tax at 20% is withheld or a treaty exemption applies, and the paying bank obtains supporting board resolutions, SARS declarations, and non-resident shareholder tax status evidence. Liquidation proceeds and surplus distributions may require prior FinSurv approval where treated as capital repatriation rather than ordinary dividends.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SARB Exchange Control Regulations, export proceeds for goods shipped by a South African resident must be received in full within 180 days from date of shipment, unless a specific extension is granted. Upon receipt, 100% of the foreign currency proceeds must be surrendered to an Authorised Dealer by conversion into ZAR unless the exporter holds a FinSurv-approved Foreign Currency Account permitting retention under defined conditions. The default statutory conversion ratio is therefore 100%; no private offshore settlement or indefinite retention of export earnings is allowed. Each export transaction must be supported by the SARS customs declaration (SAD500), transport documents, a client invoice, and proof of receipt/conversion submitted to the Authorised Dealer for compliance reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR Business Account / Inward Investment Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited acting through First National Bank (FNB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational ZAR Current Account / Foreign Currency Account
Operational Current Account / Capital Receipt Account
Business Transactional ZAR Account / Electronic Foreign Currency Account
Specialised Corporate Banking Account / Escrow and Treasury Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury banking layer for the South African entity. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not SARB Authorised Dealers and cannot lawfully provide ZAR current-account services or execute the mandatory SARB surrender of export proceeds on behalf of a South African exporter. Such platforms may be used only for ancillary inbound fee payments or payments to suppliers outside South Africa where the funds never touch the local ZAR clearing system; each use must still be reported by the South African entity to its Authorised Dealer and must avoid prohibited speculative FX activity. Any EMI operating in South Africa would need FSCA licensing and SARB financial surveillance approval, which makes full treasury substitution impracticable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (FICA) does not impose an absolute statutory requirement that all directors physically appear at a South African branch. Directors and ultimate beneficial owners must be identified, verified, and sanctioned using independently sourced or reliable electronic identity verification tools. In practice, first-time onboarding of a non-resident-owned entity requires notarised passports, proof-of-address documents, corporate beneficial ownership disclosure, and a recorded remote interview with the bank's compliance team; physical attendance may be requested by certain banks as a risk-based measure, but remote opening is accepted in South Africa if documentation is certified and the bank's board-approved onboarding policy permits it.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership chain with layered intermediate incorporation vehicles, holding companies, or discretionary trusts masking the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC-compliant register of beneficial ownership (CoR 35.2 or equivalent), full corporate organisation chart, certified certificate of incorporation for each chain entity, register of members, trust deed or written trust arrangement where applicable, passports of all ultimate natural persons, source-of-funds bank statements for the capital contribution, and board resolution approving the legal entity banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory sensitivity of the 'sterile medical device' product class, specifically whether the SAHPRA registration, sterilisation validation, and medical-device quality certifications match the export sales profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAHPRA medical device establishment licence or registration certificate for the Class II sterile nitrile examination glove, ISO 13485 certificate, ISO 11135/ISO 11137 sterilisation validation reports or batch release records, CE marking certificate or EU Notified Body certificate where exporting to regulated markets, FDA 510(k) listing where applicable, and current Good Manufacturing Practice evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency export to multiple African and offshore buyers with divergent invoice pricing creates potential trade-based money laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sales contracts, pro-forma and final commercial invoices, terminal or port bill of lading/airway bills, packing lists, inspector certificates, SARS customs SAD500 export declarations, payment confirmations, and third-party pricing benchmark analysis demonstrating arm's length export pricing consistent with comparable nitrile glove trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for offshore Foreign Currency Accounts, structured FX hedging, or payment routing through correspondent banks in third countries triggers additional exchange control and sanctions scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved board treasury policy, underlying export receivables forecast or import creditor schedule, signed ISDA or bank master derivatives agreement, counterparty and ultimate beneficial owner declarations, UN/EU/OFSI sanctions screening records, purpose and volume justification for each proposed Foreign Currency Account, and confirmation that no transaction will breach SARB surrender rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder remits subscription proceeds by SWIFT MT103 from its foreign corporate account to the South African corporate banking account held with an Authorised Dealer. The payment instruction must identify the named South African beneficiary entity, use a capital-receipt purpose code such as 'Equity Investment in South African Company' or SARB Balance of Payments reporting code for inward foreign direct investment, and include full remitter and beneficiary name details. The Authorised Dealer performs FICA checks, sanctions screening, and inward investment reporting to FinSurv, and will allocate a capital reference before releasing funds into the operational ZAR account through the SAMOS local-ZAR clearing system. A signed Share Subscription Agreement, board resolution, register of members, CIPC beneficial ownership update, and proof of source of funds must be retained. Non-resident intercompany loan capital is also permissible but must be reported to FinSurv through the Authorised Dealer, with loan agreements, interest-rate terms, and repayment schedules filed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for imported raw materials, chemicals, packaging, and production machinery should be executed through Authorised Dealer rails: direct SWIFT MT103 payment against commercial documentation, documentary collection (D/P or D/A), or commercial letters of credit issued by the South African bank via SWIFT MT700 and advised/confirmed through a correspondent bank. For large contracted supplier purchases, an irrevocable confirmed commercial LC is preferred because it simultaneously protects the exporter and gives the issuing bank documented trade evidence. The Authorised Dealer requires the commercial invoice, transport documents, packing list, insurance certificate, SARS customs SAD500 import declaration, and, where applicable, evidence of customs duty payment. Advance payments are permitted only with supporting pro-forma invoices and bank-guarantee triggers; import settlement is ordinarily expected within 180 days of shipment and any rollover requires bank justification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR forward exchange contracts (FX forwards) with an SARB Authorised Dealer, executed only against documented current-account or approved capital-account underlying exposures.
Cross-currency swaps between ZAR and the trade currency used to hedge both principal and interest cash flows on approved offshore funding or material import/export receivables.
FX option collars and risk reversals used as a hedge on anticipated export revenue, provided the instrument neutralises the underlying currency risk and contains no speculative open position.

Onshore ZAR non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where expressly approved by FinSurv or accepted as an institutionally available instrument for qualifying non-resident counterparties; ordinary resident operating-entity hedging uses deliverable forwards instead.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary each year; filing window opens 3 months before the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts CIPC administrative late-return penalties; continued default triggers a CIPC final warning notice and administrative deregistration under section 82 of the Companies Act. Upon deregistration, the company loses legal capacity and assets vest in a curator or the State, and directors may be personally liable for obligations incurred after strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed and filed together with the CIPC Annual Return; any registrable shareholding transfer must be reflected in the Beneficial Ownership Register and filed with CIPC without undue delay.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or file the Beneficial Ownership Register is a continuing compliance offence under the Companies Amendment / General Laws Amendment Act; CIPC may reject the annual return, impose administrative penalties, pursue deregistration, and expose officers to fines and imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 12 months after the company's financial year-end; provisional tax payments fall due in two or three interim instalments during and after the year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission triggers SARS administrative penalties (up to ZAR 250 per month per registration, capped), understatement penalties, interest on unpaid tax, and possible estimated assessments followed by civil tax debt enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered where the company's Public Interest Score equals or exceeds 350, or where the company is a public company, state-owned company, or a private company that a shareholder or regulator lawfully directs to be audited. Private companies with a Public Interest Score between 100 and 349 may satisfy the Companies Act by an independent review unless an audit is otherwise required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), with IFRS for SMEs permitted for qualifying non-public companies under the Companies Act regulations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register identifying each natural person who directly or indirectly exercises control or holds 5% or more of shares. The CIPC Annual Return requires confirmation that this register is complete and current. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the register and filed with CIPC as part of the annual confirmation cycle and updated on an ongoing basis.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150–400 typical annual fee for registered office / CIPC compliance agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000–6,000 typical for a mid-size private manufacturing company; independent review, when permitted, is notably lower

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for qualifying Special Economic Zone (SEZ) companies; 150% super-deduction for approved research and development under Section 11D; accelerated wear-and-tear allowances on qualifying manufacturing assets; learnership allowances under Section 12H; urban development zone deductions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory time limit (subject to anti-loss-trading continuity rules under Section 20A)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) submitted electronically via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months of the company's financial year-end, unless SARS prescribes an earlier issue date in the notice for that year of assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income - all local and foreign-source income received by or accrued to the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only South African-source income unless a foreign tax credit or exemption applies under a Double Taxation Agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income - dividends received (subject to dividend tax), government compensation, and qualifying interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest and royalties sourced in South Africa are exempt where a treaty provision or specific exemption applies; attach proof of exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income - gross income less allowable deductions, recoupments, and assessed losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses directly attributable to South African-source gross income; apportionment rules apply for mixed-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss from prior years claimed as a deduction in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident may claim carried-forward assessed losses only if the loss was mathematically derived from South African-source income and the continuity-of-trade test is satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed tax - taxable income multiplied by the company tax rate (27%), subject to turnover-based small business rate concessions if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty-limitation or reduced SEZ rate where the company qualifies; do not reduce tax unless authoritative treaty relief is on file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rebates and deferred tax - includes foreign tax credits, assessed-loss offsets, and provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies can credit foreign tax on South African-source income only up to the South African normal tax payable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Section 210 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, a monthly administrative penalty may be imposed for late filing; the maximum is ZAR 16,400 per month or up to 40% of the assessed tax for large companies. Interest accrues on unpaid tax at 10.25% per annum. Criminal liability for intentional non-filing is possible under Section 234.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 (Provisional Tax Return) filed via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Six-monthly (two mandatory provisional periods per year of assessment)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional payment due within the first 6 months of the year of assessment; second payment due on or before the final day of the year of assessment; a third voluntary top-up payment may be made within 6 months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic amount - the last assessed taxable income, used to estimate the provisional taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident has no South African assessed history, the basic amount must be conservatively estimated based on the expected South African-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated taxable income for the current year - must be a reasonable estimate based on available financial information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income subject to South African normal tax; exclude treaty-exempt income; disregard temporary timing differences in the absence of a SARS confirmation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax payable - 27% of estimated taxable income less any applicable rebates; payments are made in two installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident payors must pay provisional tax before any dividend or interest is distributed if the underlying earnings are South African-source and not fully subjected to withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late/non-payment of provisional tax triggers interest under section 89quat of the Income Tax Act. Additionally, if the estimated taxable income is materially understated (i.e., less than 90% of actual), a 15% to 20% penalty may be imposed under paragraph 20 of the Fourth Schedule.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (Dividend Tax under Section 64E of the Income Tax Act)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The paying company must withhold South African dividend tax at 20% unless the non-resident beneficial owner submits to the payor an approved SARS declaration and a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, confirming residency in a treaty jurisdiction. The declaration must be received before the dividend is paid, and the payor must retain the declaration and TRC for five years. SARS may require the beneficial owner to provide a statement of economic substance in cross-border avoidance cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 15% (Section 50A), royalties 15% (Section 49B). Under DTA networks, interest is commonly reduced to 0% (e.g., US treaty) and royalties to 5%-10%; a 0% rate may apply to interest derived by financial institutions depending on the treaty. Treaty benefits are denied where the recipient is a 'conduit' or lacks beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country Report mandatory for MNE groups with consolidated group revenue ≥ ZAR 10 billion; Local File and Master File documentation expected where the aggregate value of cross-border connected-person transactions exceeds ZAR 5 million. Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be prepared for every cross-border transaction falling within those thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations, but the common-law 'substance over form' doctrine, the controlled foreign company rules (Section 9D), and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (Sections 80A-80L) of the Income Tax Act are applied. A domiciled shell company with minimal substance will be disregarded for residency and treaty-access purposes, and its income may be re-characterised as flowing to the real controlling foreign entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating turnover, fabricating invoices, omitting foreign-source income, or mischaracterising royalties as service fees to avoid South African tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Section 235 of the Tax Administration Act, intentional tax evasion is a criminal offence punishable by a fine of up to ZAR 1 million or imprisonment for up to five years. Section 234 imposes a separate penalty of up to two years' imprisonment for knowingly making false statements in a tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed under Section 9 of the Tax Administration Act when a company's failure to pay tax results from negligence, fraud, or illegal acts committed with the director's knowledge or consent. Civil damages, travel bans, and criminal imprisonment apply on conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an entity with no physical office, no employees, no decision-making capacity, or entering into circular transactions that serve only to access treaty benefits or shift profits out of South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS will disregard the entity's separate existence under the substance-over-form doctrine; the income is re-attributed to the beneficial owner. An additional 'conduit-company' penalty of 100% of the tax evaded may be levied under Section 223, and administrative penalties and interest accrue from the due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who set up a shell entity to evade tax become jointly and severally liable for the entire tax deficiency, plus penalties and interest. A court may issue a personal travel ban and order restitution of assets transferred to offshore accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register as an accountable institution under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA), not conducting customer due diligence (including beneficial-ownership verification), or failing to report suspicious transactions linked to medical PPE procurement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FICA imposes administrative penalties of up to ZAR 10 million per breach on a company; criminal sanctions include a fine of up to ZAR 100 million or imprisonment up to 15 years for wilful non-compliance and money laundering offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are presumed to be responsible for institutional AML failures; personal fines up to ZAR 10 million, civil disqualification from directorship, and extradition-compatible criminal charges can be pursued. Travel bans are routinely imposed pending investigation.
